welcome.body: This is the Kopher Shield NOC panel: real-time integrity, traffic and backup history. Let's take a quick tour of the main areas.
welcome.title: Welcome to your Digital Fortress

sidebar.body: All of Kopher Shield is one click away. When you continue, we will open the Routines screen for you.
sidebar.title: Navigation menu

routines.body: Schedule backups and define parallel (multithread) execution, compression and retention policies. Each routine shows its status, progress and next run.
routines.title: Routines and multithread policies

cloud.body: Manage your storage providers (Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2 and more). Each vault shows its live connection status.
cloud.title: Cloud Vaults

audit.body: Every action is recorded in immutable, tamper-proof logs, ready for compliance and forensic investigation. That completes the tour!
audit.title: Immutable audit

multithread.title: Multithread Backup Policies
multithread.intro: The Kopher Shield engine processes files in parallel, spreading work across several threads to shorten the backup window without saturating the machine.

blocks.p: Under Routines, click New Routine, set the source folder, the destination vault (local or cloud) and the schedule (manual, daily, weekly or monthly).
Each file is split into blocks, encrypted with AES-256 and uploaded in parallel. Run several routines at once with Select Batch.
Progress is shown in real time on each routine. If a run fails, the red Failed tag shows the reason on hover.

multithread.tip: Schedule heavy backups outside business hours to preserve server performance.

cloud.title: Cloud Vaults & S3 Keys
cloud.intro: A Cloud Vault is an S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Backblaze) where encrypted blocks are stored outside your network.

blocks.p: Under Cloud Vaults, enter the name, endpoint, bucket, Access Key and Secret Key. Keys are kept in the backend only and never exposed in the UI.
Create a dedicated key for Kopher Shield with read/write permission on the bucket only, and rotate it regularly.
Enable Object Lock (WORM) on the bucket to prevent deletion or tampering of backups, even during a ransomware attack.

cloud.tip: Never reuse cloud account admin keys in a vault.

restore.title: Restore Process
restore.intro: Restore rebuilds your files from a .kophershield manifest, verifying the integrity of each block before writing.

blocks.p: Under Restore, pick the local or cloud vault and wait for the available manifests to load.
Each manifest is a point in time. Choose the one you need and set the recovery destination folder.
Blocks are decrypted and hash-verified. Restore to an alternate folder first to check the data before replacing originals.

restore.tip: Test restores regularly: a backup is only trustworthy once it has been restored successfully.

audit.title: Audit & Compliance
audit.intro: Every relevant action is recorded in an immutable log, supporting requirements such as GDPR and ISO 27001.

blocks.p: Routine runs, failures, restores, configuration changes and administrative access, always timestamped.
Under Audit, filter by level and search by text. The table is virtualized and handles tens of thousands of records without slowdown.
Records are append-only, cannot be edited by users, and can be exported as evidence for external audits.

audit.tip: Export logs regularly and store them according to your retention policy.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
faq.q0: How do I restore files from a local vault?
faq.a0: Go to the "Restore" menu, select the vault folder, pick the matching manifest and click "Run Restore".
faq.q1: What if a scheduled routine fails?
faq.a1: Check the Audit screen for the detailed error log and make sure the data source has read permission.
faq.q2: How do I renew or change the enterprise license key?
faq.a2: Go to "Settings" > "Licensing" to update your activation key or manage two-factor authentication (2FA) tokens.
